increment_paragraph: **RETURN-FAMILY-UNTRACKED-REVERSED-SUBSCRIPT** (USER DECISION 2026-11-24: "launch the two arithmetic-access follow-up cards"; gateway rule 74y, extending rule 74w; `QCore.ReturnFamilyUntrackedReversedSubscript`; [report](../../reports/return-family-untracked-reversed-subscript/README.md)). C11 6.5.2.1p2 defines `E1[E2]` as `(*((E1)+(E2)))`, so the pointer a subscript dereferences may stand inside its brackets, but family S of `legacy_return_family` read a root as a subscript base only as `p [`. So `long w(long k) { const long *p = 0; return 1[p]; }`, `k[p]`, `k[(const long *)p]`, `0[p + k]` and `(k + 1)[p]` were `Safe`, while `return p[1];` is `Unknown` (`unknown_alias:p`); and `long w(long **q, long n) { return n[*q]; }` admitted the may-bind `q` as one dereference although the subscript dereferences the value `*q` reads. The old tests are kept and `subscript_index` adds one: it widens a span from an untracked, non-scalar root as rule 74w's walk does and, when the span fills a subscript's brackets (alone or as a term of a sum there), makes the root a base unless the subscripted operand is a name the declaration reader declares as a pointer or array (`NameFacts::declared_pointer`, `FunctionTypes::pointer_kind`; never a member name). An undecided operand makes both bases; an unclassified sum in the brackets refuses. A may-bind root inside a `[` whose subscripted operand is not a declared pointer refuses (`inside_undecided_subscript`), which closes RETURN-FAMILY-SUBSCRIPT-ENCLOSING-STARRED-ROOT without rule 74s's code. Bases only grow and the new refusals are the expression's, so nothing admits more than at the base (`the_fix_only_refuses_more`); the Lean model also proves from the subscript's definition that the reader never reads an inside pointer as an index (`an_inside_pointer_is_never_missed`). `p[i]`, `a[i]` with a declared array, tracked roots, unbound formals, `&k[p]` and `sizeof(k[p])` read as before; after `k_free(q)`, `return 0[*q];` moves from `Unsafe` to the return refusal. Pinned at unit level (`subscriptVectors`, 20 rows, and `mayBindVectors`, 9 rows) and end to end (12 null rows, 2 unclassified refusals, 3 may-bind refusals, controls); rule 74w's unit pin holding `a [ p + 1 ]` at `bases: [a]` under an oracle that declares no pointer now expects the union. The change pins fail with the new reading disabled. Opt-in `current --monkey-linked` over Fluent Bit 046accf6: no row moves (1,171 / 2 / 3,623 / 8 at both), as predicted; the census found no reversed subscript on the route, and its ordinary `X[i]` hits keep their readings. The pinned routes need inputs this host lacks and were not run.

ledger.why: Discharged by RETURN-FAMILY-UNTRACKED-REVERSED-SUBSCRIPT (rule 74y). Reachability: `long w(long k) { const long *p = 0; return 1[p]; }`, `k[p]`, `k[(const long *)p]`, `k[(p)]`, `0[p + k]`, `k[p + 1]`, `1[(const long *)p + k]`, `0[(p + 1)]`, `(k + 1)[p]` and `0[p].n` reached family S and were `Safe` at the base 03aadb221 (report §1). crates/qcore-c-gateway/src/legacy_return_family.rs keeps every old test and adds `subscript_index`: it widens a span from an untracked, non-scalar root through type groups (the existing `type_group_open`), parentheses and rule 74w's additive groups, and when the span fills a subscript's brackets the root is a base unless the subscripted operand is a declared pointer or array (`NameFacts::declared_pointer`, read from `FunctionTypes::pointer_kind`; a member name never is). An undecided operand makes both bases; a crossed sum rule 74w would not classify refuses the expression. Bases only grow and the new refusals are the expression's, so a result the tip admits the base admitted (`QCore.ReturnFamilyUntrackedReversedSubscript.the_fix_only_refuses_more`, `old_base_kept`); grounded in C11 6.5.2.1p2 (`subscript_comm`, `an_inside_pointer_is_never_missed`). The null cases are pinned `Unknown` (`unknown_alias:p`) end to end (crates/qcore-c-gateway/tests/return_family_untracked_reversed_subscript.rs); unbound formals stay `Safe`, and `p[1]`, a declared array or pointer subscripted by a non-scalar index, `&k[p]`, `sizeof(k[p])` and a tracked root keep their verdicts. The unit vectors bind the Lean rows, and the change pins fail with the new reading disabled. The opt-in corpus measurement shows no move, as predicted (report §5). The pinned routes need inputs this host lacks and were not run.

Discharged by RETURN-FAMILY-UNTRACKED-REVERSED-SUBSCRIPT (rule 74y), the same shape as the reversed subscript: which side of a subscript is the pointer. `long w(long **q, long n) { return n[*q]; }` and `n[*q + 1]` reached family S and were `Safe` at the base 03aadb221, and after `k_free(q)` `return 0[*q];` was `Unsafe` (report §1). crates/qcore-c-gateway/src/legacy_return_family.rs adds `inside_undecided_subscript`: a may-bind root of any admitted shape (`* q`, `q - > f`, `q [ i ]`) is refused when a `[` enclosing it subscripts an operand that is not a declared pointer or array, because the bracket's value may then be the pointer the subscript dereferences, computed from the value the root's one dereference reads. `a[*q]` with a declared array `a` keeps its admission, as the DISCHARGE asks. The check needs none of rule 74s's code (`outside_dereference`, `group_dereferenced`); the two refusals are independent. The admission is the base's conjoined with that condition, so nothing admits more (`QCore.ReturnFamilyUntrackedReversedSubscript.admitted_was_admitted`, `the_fix_only_refuses_more`). `return n[*q];`, `n[*q + 1]` and the released `0[*q]` are pinned as the return refusal end to end (crates/qcore-c-gateway/tests/return_family_untracked_reversed_subscript.rs) and at unit level (`mayBindVectors`), and the change pins fail with the new reading disabled. The opt-in corpus measurement shows no move, as predicted (report §5).
